faults.fault: Box fit not credible and by its own numbers violated: width stack gives wheels only 0.04 m per side, yet the sinkage calc uses wheel width b=0.15 m (outboard wheels -> 0.32+2x0.15=0.62 m > 0.5 m); the height stack (0.42 m) contains no wheels (~0.33 m dia by scale bar) and no tub body, so tucking wheels under adds >=0.33 m (>0.5 m). No arrangement of four 0.33x0.15 m wheels fits the stated 0.1/0.1/0.08 m margins.
faults.checked_by: Re-summed the stacks; compared b=0.15 m in Bekker calc and 0.12 m2 contact area (0.03 m2/wheel needs >=0.75 m contact length at 0.04 m width); wheel diameter measured against ~200 mm scale bar

faults.fault: Contact area 0.12 m2 is inconsistent with its own result: a ~0.33 m rigid wheel sinking 4 mm has a contact chord ~0.07 m, so 4x0.15x0.07 ~0.044 m2; real pressure ~2.7x higher (~8.7 kPa empty) and sinkage larger.

The transfer conveyor runs downhill from the ladder top and ends at deck level below and beside the hopper; the hopper mouth is ~0.25 m higher. Soil would have to jump up into the hopper; the text says the belt lifts it in.

faults.fault: 933 N is hub-motor torque force (4x35 N m/0.15 m), not soil traction. With its own 13.9 kg mass, weight is 136 N, so traction ~55-80 N is below the 40-85 N vibrated draft. Drawbar ratio and pressure use 589 N (60 kg), so the '>10x margin' is false.
The person is about as tall as the robot frame; by the 200 mm scale bar he is ~0.95 m tall, and the wheels are ~0.42 m vs 300 mm stated.

b1.better_why: A and B tie on total, but A re-derives its deciding numbers (mass, cut vs traction, fill, power, thermal, stop) and its faults are packaging and drawing errors. B's core dig rate is 15x off and digging BP-1 is unchecked. C fails at its core soil transfer and its envelope.

faults.fault: The 60 W fan is counted only as heat divided by COP, not as direct electricity: electric = 376/2.5+60 = 210 W -> 5.05 kWh/day; with the 200 kg batch that is 7.05 of 8.1 kWh PV (87%, not 69%); night 2.94 kWh = 57% of battery; holding autonomy ~1.0 day, not 1.42.
The ~1000 mm scale bar (~145 px) makes the box ~5 m tall; against the person the box is ~3 m tall and the door ~2.5 m, vs a stated 2.2 m box and 900 mm door.
faults.checked_by: Pixel measurement of person, box, door and bar

faults.fault: No solar/radiant gain on a sun-exposed box in a hot region; 80 W infiltration with door openings in ~40 C air is unsupported.
~60 crates in a 1.8x1.8x2.0 m interior with a centre aisle and 'low' racks needs ~6 levels; the packing is not shown; the picture shows ~15 crates (cutaway).
Specific heat used inconsistently (25 kWh implies 3.6 kJ/kgK x 25 K; buffer uses 3.5); autonomy uses 100% battery depth.
Cold air drawn spilling out beneath the box onto the plinth; measurement chain only two boxes.

C1.why: Solar-only daily balance and night battery are computed, and 1 tonne holding with an honest 200 kg/day intake cap; still met after correcting the fan term.

C2.why: Standard PV, LiFePO4, DC chiller and PU room; conduction 186 W re-derives, and the pull-down limit is recognised.

C3.why: Nearly all arithmetic re-derives, but the fan electricity omission understates daily energy and night draw by ~40%.

C5.why: Off-the-shelf and honest about pull-down exceeding PV and the intake cap.

C8.why: Clean, legible, correct panel count; scale bar error is a picture fault.

faults.fault: No heat-load calculation; 2.0-2.5 kW thermal and 7-9 kWh/day are asserted from precedents. Own envelope: U 0.2 x 26 m2 x 33 K ~173 W conduction, ~3 kWh/day holding; pull-down 24 kWh thermal re-derives.
10-12.5 kWh/day from 2.5 kWp x 4-5 h ignores system losses; at ~75% it is 7.5-9.4 kWh against a 7-9 kWh need, no margin left for ice-making.

faults.where: How it works / Parts: ice bank
faults.fault: A 4-8 C DC monoblock cannot freeze water; it needs a sub-zero evaporator or a second circuit. Freezing 200-300 kg needs 18.6-27.8 kWh thermal, more than the whole PV budget; the charge/discharge path is not described.

Half the box is an equipment bay inside the insulated envelope (chiller, battery, tanks) with no outside heat rejection; the produce room is shown about one crate wide holding ~10 crates, not 40 crates in 2.4x1.8 m; cold-air arrows pass through the partition and spill out under the box.
2.4x1.8x2.1 m = 9.1 m3, not ~7 m3; '658W/h' unit garble; battery 10 kWh vs 7-10 kWh.
Ice-bank tanks drawn as pressure gas cylinders; no scale bar or labels.

C1.why: Solar-only and 1 tonne are claimed from precedents; the energy balance is not closed with losses.

C2.why: PV-battery chiller room works, but the ice bank as described cannot be charged by the stated chiller.

C3.why: No load calculation; optimistic PV; ice-bank energy not budgeted; only the pull-down figure re-derives.

C4.why: Unlabelled, no scale; the produce room is far smaller than stated, and the machinery sits inside the cold envelope.

C5.why: Off-the-shelf and cites real precedents, with honest risks, but key performance is asserted.

C6.why: Readable concept narrative; ice-bank and airflow mechanism unexplained.

C7.why: Specific steps (galvanised skid, cam-lock PIR panels, R290 vacuum test, commissioning).

C8.why: Airflow through walls and out of the box, gas-cylinder tanks, interior inconsistent with the stated room.

02.better_why: A closes a computed load and energy budget (with one fixable fan-electricity error) and honestly caps warm intake. B asserts loads from precedents, overstates PV yield, has an ice bank its chiller cannot charge, and its picture contradicts the stated room.
